bank.explanation: A red circle with a white horizontal bar means 'No Entry'. A red circle with a blue background and a red cross means 'No Waiting' or 'Clearway'
A circular sign with a blue background and a white arrow pointing to the left or right indicates that vehicles must pass that way
bank.question: A blue circular sign with a white arrow signifies a mandatory direction that must be followed

bank.explanation: An upside-down triangle (Give Way) is a regulatory sign, not a warning sign. Warning signs are almost always upward-pointing triangles with red borders
bank.question: All triangular road signs with a red border are used to provide warnings about potential hazards ahead
Direction signs with a brown background are used to lead drivers to tourist attractions
bank.explanation: Brown backdrops are specifically reserved for pointing road users toward tourist attractions, zoos, or heritage sites
Double yellow lines mean no waiting at any time, regardless of whether there are upright signs present
bank.question: Double yellow lines only apply during daylight hours unless a nearby sign specifies otherwise
Direction signs on primary routes have a green background
bank.explanation: Green backgrounds are used for primary routes, while white backgrounds with black borders are used for non-primary or local roads
An amber light means you must stop unless you have already crossed the stop line or are too close to stop safely without causing an accident
bank.question: When a traffic light turns amber, you should always accelerate to clear the junction before it turns red

bank.explanation: A black horizontal line on a yellow background (usually on a square sign) indicates the height of a bridge or overhead obstruction
bank.question: A 'T' shape symbol on a road sign indicates a 'No Through Road'

bank.explanation: The national speed limit for a car on a single carriageway is 60 mph. 70 mph applies to dual carriageways and motorways
bank.question: The national speed limit for a motor car on a single carriageway road is 70 mph

bank.explanation: Zig-zag lines (white at crossings, yellow at schools) mean no stopping or parking at any time to preserve visibility for pedestrians
bank.question: You are permitted to park on white zig-zag lines near a pedestrian crossing as long as your hazard lights are on

bank.explanation: Blue rectangular signs are used to provide information on motorways, such as exit numbers and distances
bank.question: Information signs on motorways have a blue background
A solid white line at the edge of the road is used to show the edge of the carriageway
bank.explanation: A solid white line down the side of the road marks the edge of the carriageway, helping drivers see the road layout in the dark or fog

bank.question: A circular sign with a red border and a blank white centre means that all vehicles are prohibited
bank.explanation: A red circle with no symbols inside is the standard sign for 'No vehicles,' meaning all vehicles are prohibited from entering

bank.question: The national speed limit for a car on a dual carriageway is 60 mph
bank.explanation: The national speed limit for a car on a dual carriageway is 70 mph, whereas it is 60 mph on a single carriageway

bank.question: The 'Stop' sign is the only UK road sign that is circular in shape
bank.explanation: Stop signs are the only road signs in the UK that are octagonal, specifically designed to be recognisable even if covered in snow
A red cross over a blue circle signifies 'No Stopping' (Clearway); the 'No Waiting' sign has a single diagonal red line
bank.question: A blue circular sign with a red border and two diagonal red lines forming a cross means 'No Waiting'
Temporary information signs for roadworks usually have a yellow background
bank.explanation: In the UK, signs with a yellow background and black lettering are used to provide temporary information about roadworks or diversions

bank.question: A triangular warning sign with a black 'X' symbol in the middle indicates a T-junction ahead
bank.explanation: A red triangle with a black 'X' signifies a crossroads; a 'T-junction' is represented by a 'T' shaped symbol

bank.question: You should not enter an area of hatched white lines bounded by a broken white line unless it is necessary and safe
bank.explanation: White diagonal stripes bounded by a broken white line should not be entered unless it is necessary and safe to do so
These markings warn drivers that they are approaching a hazard or a continuous solid white line
bank.question: Longer white paint lines with shorter gaps in the centre of the road indicate a hazard ahead
A rectangular blue sign with a white 'P' and a bicycle symbol means the area is for car parking only
bank.explanation: A blue rectangle with a white 'P' and a motorcycle symbol indicates parking for motorcycles only

bank.question: You must not enter a yellow box junction unless your exit is clear, except when turning right and being prevented from doing so by oncoming traffic
bank.explanation: Box junctions are marked with yellow criss-cross lines and you must not enter unless your exit is clear
A 'Give Way' sign is a downward-pointing triangle with a red border; it is the only triangle sign that points downwards
bank.question: A 'Give Way' sign is an upward-pointing triangle with a red border
Yellow zig-zag markings outside of a school mean that you must not park or stop there at any time
bank.explanation: Zig-zag lines (yellow or white) are placed near crossings and schools to provide a clear view for both pedestrians and drivers
Red circles are regulatory and generally tell you what you must not do, while blue circles usually give a mandatory instruction
bank.question: Road signs that give orders are generally circular in shape
Direction signs on motorways have a brown background
bank.explanation: A brown background is used specifically for signs providing directions to tourist attractions and facilities

bank.question: The 'camera' symbol on a sign can be used to indicate areas where speed cameras or 'average speed' checks are in operation
bank.explanation: This gives an early warning to drivers that their speed is being monitored in the area

bank.question: A circular sign with a red border and a red cross on a blue background means 'No Stopping' (Clearway)
bank.explanation: The clearway sign means you must not stop on the main carriageway for any reason except in an emergency
A single yellow line means no waiting during the times shown on a nearby sign; the restriction is not always 24/7
bank.question: A single yellow line along the side of the road means 'No Waiting' at any time
A circular sign with a red border and a picture of a car and a motorcycle means 'Only motor vehicles allowed'
bank.explanation: This sign (a car over a motorbike) means 'No motor vehicles' (all motor vehicles are prohibited)

bank.question: The 'Give Way' sign is the only UK road sign that is an upside-down triangle
bank.explanation: The inverted triangle allows drivers to identify the sign even if it is covered by snow or dirt
On a motorway, the studs between the hard shoulder and the carriageway are red to help drivers identify the edge of the road in low visibility
bank.question: Red reflective studs (cat's eyes) are used to mark the left-hand edge of the motorway
A traffic light sequence showing both Red and Amber together means you can go if the way is clear
bank.explanation: When the amber and red lights are shown together, you must wait for the green light before you move off

bank.question: Hatched white lines bounded by a solid white line must not be entered except in an emergency
bank.explanation: These lines are used to discourage overtaking or to protect traffic turning right where the view is restricted

bank.question: White reflective studs are used to mark the right-hand edge of the carriageway on a motorway
bank.explanation: White studs are used to mark the lanes or the middle of the road, not the right-hand edge of a motorway

bank.question: A triangular sign with a red border showing two children walking signifies 'School Crossing' or 'Children' ahead
bank.explanation: This sign is often found near schools or playgrounds where children are likely to be crossing

bank.question: On directional signs, a green background indicates that you are on a primary route
bank.explanation: Green backgrounds are used for primary routes, whereas white backgrounds with black borders are used for non-primary or local routes

bank.question: A circular sign with a red border containing both a car and a motorcycle means motor vehicles are allowed
bank.explanation: This sign means 'no motor vehicles'. Both cars and motorcycles are prohibited from entering past this sign

bank.question: A single yellow line means you must not wait during the times shown on the accompanying sign
bank.explanation: A single yellow line indicates waiting restrictions apply at certain times; you must check the nearby plate for specific hours

bank.question: Green reflective studs are used to mark the boundary between the edge of the motorway and the central reservation
bank.explanation: Amber studs mark the right-hand edge of the carriageway next to a central reservation. Green studs mark slip road exits or entries

bank.question: The ‘STOP’ sign is the only road sign in the UK that has an octagonal shape
bank.explanation: The 'STOP' sign is uniquely octagonal to ensure it is recognizable even if the face of the sign is covered in snow or dirt

bank.question: A circular sign with a blue background and no red border generally gives a warning of a hazard ahead
bank.explanation: Signs with blue circles but no red borders are mandatory signs that give positive instructions, such as 'turn left ahead'
Double white lines where the line nearest to you is solid mean you must not cross or straddle it, except in very specific limited circumstances
bank.question: You must not cross a solid white line in the centre of the road if the line nearest to you is solid

bank.explanation: Signs for tourist attractions and facilities use a brown background with white lettering and symbols
bank.question: Information signs for tourist attractions in the UK are typically shown with a black background

bank.explanation: The sign with a car falling off a pier into water actually warns of a 'quayside or river bank' ahead
bank.question: A triangular warning sign showing a car falling into water indicates that the road ahead is prone to flooding

bank.explanation: The 'National Speed Limit' sign is a white circle with a single black diagonal stripe. On a single carriageway, this limit is 60mph for cars
bank.question: The 'National Speed Limit' sign consists of a black diagonal stripe on a white circular background
Information signs on motorways, such as those indicating the start of the motorway, are usually rectangular and blue
bank.explanation: Blue rectangular signs are used to inform road users of various features, such as the start of a motorway or a bus lane

bank.question: A 'Red X' displayed on a gantry above a motorway lane means you should stay in that lane but slow down
bank.explanation: The red cross on a white background (Red X) above a motorway lane means that lane is closed and you must not drive in it

bank.question: A circular sign with a red border and a bicycle symbol means 'No Cycling'
bank.explanation: A circular sign with a red border and a bicycle inside indicates that cycling is prohibited in that area

bank.question: Information signs for tourist attractions in the UK are typically shown with a green background
bank.explanation: Brown signs are used to provide directions to tourist attractions, such as zoos, museums, or historic houses

bank.question: Yellow reflective studs are used to mark the boundary between the slip road and the main motorway
bank.explanation: Yellow studs are used to mark the edge of the carriageway adjacent to the central reservation on a motorway

bank.question: The 'No Entry' sign for vehicular traffic is a red circle with a white horizontal bar
bank.explanation: The 'No Entry' sign is a red circle with a horizontal white bar through the middle

bank.question: You must not park on white zig-zag lines found at the approach to a pedestrian crossing
bank.explanation: Zig-zag lines near pedestrian crossings are there to ensure clear visibility for both pedestrians and drivers

bank.question: A circular sign with a red border containing a 'T' shape indicates a T-junction ahead
bank.explanation: T-junction signs are triangular warning signs; circular signs with red borders are used to give orders (prohibitions)
The flashing amber light means you must give way to pedestrians already on the crossing, but you may proceed if it is clear
bank.question: At a pelican crossing, a flashing amber light means you must give way to pedestrians on the crossing
A circular sign with a red border and the number '30' inside indicates a minimum speed limit of 30 mph
bank.explanation: The 'Minimum Speed' sign is a blue circle with white numerals; a red border signifies a 'Maximum' speed limit
Green studs mark the edge of the main carriageway where it crosses the entrance or exit of a slip road
bank.question: Green reflective studs are used to indicate that there are roadworks ahead on a motorway

bank.explanation: A blue rectangular sign with a white 'P' and a motorcycle symbol indicates a parking area reserved specifically for motorcycles
bank.question: A blue rectangular sign with a white 'P' and a motorcycle symbol indicates a parking area for motorcycles only

bank.explanation: This specific sign is used to warn drivers that the dual carriageway is ending and they are entering a road with two-way traffic
bank.question: A triangular sign with two arrows pointing in opposite directions (up and down) indicates two-way traffic ahead

bank.explanation: Double white lines where the line nearest to you is broken mean you may cross to overtake if it is safe to do so
bank.question: You are never allowed to cross double white lines in the centre of the road, even if the line closest to you is broken

bank.explanation: A red circle with a black 'car' and 'motorcycle' symbol means all motor vehicles are prohibited from entering that area
bank.question: A circular sign with a red border containing no numbers and only symbols of a car and a motorcycle means motor vehicles are prohibited

bank.explanation: Red studs are used to mark the left-hand edge of the running lane, while amber studs are used to mark the edge of the central reservation
bank.question: On a motorway, amber reflective studs are used to mark the left-hand edge of the carriageway
Road signs in the shape of a diamond are specifically intended for tram drivers
bank.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are specifically designed to provide instructions and warnings to tram drivers, not general motorists
A signs ends with a red diagonal line through it, but the base sign for a 'Clearway' is a blue circle with a red border and a red cross (X), not a black circle
bank.question: A 'Clearway' sign, which prohibits stopping at any time, is a black circle with a red cross
You may cross a solid white line in the centre of the road to overtake a horse-drawn vehicle, provided it is travelling at 10 mph or less
bank.explanation: You may cross a solid white line to pass a stationary vehicle, or to overtake a pedal cycle, horse, or road maintenance vehicle travelling at 10 mph or less
